artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Steven Wilson's The Overview, released on March 14, 2025, via Fiction Records, is his eighth solo studio album and marks a deliberate return to progressive rock after exploring more electronic sounds in his previous works. The album is a concept piece inspired by the "overview effect," a cognitive shift experienced by astronauts viewing Earth from space, which shapes its expansive and atmospheric musical style. It consists of two lengthy tracks totaling around 42 minutes—"Objects Outlive Us" and the title track "The Overview"—each composed of multiple distinct sections that flow seamlessly, blending classic prog influences like Pink Floyd and Tangerine Dream with modern elements such as glistening electronics and post-rock textures.

Musically, The Overview updates the progressive rock genre for the 21st century, combining intricate arrangements with a cinematic scope. The album features collaborations with musicians including Craig Blundell on drums and keyboardist Adam Holzman, and includes lyrics by Andy Partridge of XTC on a section of "Objects Outlive Us". Thematically, it explores humanity's place in the universe and the contrasting perspectives of awe and insignificance inspired by space observation. Critically, the album has been noted for its ambitious structure and conceptual depth, with Wilson himself describing it as his most audacious work to date. It was premiered alongside a commissioned film at the BFI IMAX in London, underscoring its multimedia and immersive nature. Commercially, it continues Wilson’s strong presence in the progressive rock scene, supported by his first solo tour in over seven years starting in May 2025.
